Architecture and Ownership

Application composition

src/main.py builds the FastAPI application, mounts the domain routers, serves the committed Dashboard and Website assets, and configures lifecycle behavior. src/api_docs.py publishes separate OpenAPI contracts so each public API surface can evolve without relying on the combined legacy schema.

The backend has three main areas:

Area Owns Key code
Community Proposals, reviewer applications, reviews, GitHub synchronization, and outbound deliveries src/community/
Control panel Benchmark plans and runs, execution backends, task data, and worker-facing APIs src/control_panel/
Shared runtime Configuration, authentication, database sessions/models, and cross-domain jobs src/core/, src/db/, src/jobs/

Community and control-panel schemas and services belong to their domains. The database is shared. src/jobs/runner.py orchestrates queued community and v1 work; Harbor v2 has its own runner under src/control_panel/v2/.

API contracts

The current separately versioned API surfaces are:

Surface Swagger UI OpenAPI JSON
Community v1 /docs/community/v1 /openapi/community/v1.json
EC2 control panel v1 /docs/ec2/v1 /openapi/ec2/v1.json
Harbor EC2 v2 /docs/ec2/v2 /openapi/ec2/v2.json

/docs and /openapi.json remain the combined legacy surface for existing consumers. When changing an API, update the owning schema/route and its contract-level documentation together.

Persistence and migrations

ORM models and database session setup live under src/db/. Alembic settings are in alembic.ini; versioned schema changes live in migrations/versions/. Do not treat a model-only change as a complete schema change: add and review a migration, and keep upgrade behavior aligned with supported existing databases.

Frontend assets

Dashboard source is in dashboard-frontend/frontend/; its Vite build is committed to src/static/. The public Website source is the ai4s-bench-website/ submodule, while its deployable snapshot is src/website_dist/. Follow the build and submodule workflow in backend/README.md when updating either asset set.

The backend serves that committed Website snapshot at /website-preview/. Push Website changes to the configured fork, stage the parent gitlink, and run python scripts/sync_website_preview.py before committing the snapshot in the parent PR. The Website source PR can remain open; the official GitHub Pages site does not need to update before a backend preview release. Production deploys the merged parent-main commit with deploy/deploy.sh on EC2. See Runtime and Configuration for that entry point and the deployment sequence.

Change checklist

For a behavior change, identify the owning domain, update the route/schema or service, review persistence and migrations if data changes, and update this wiki when the interface or operational behavior changes. Existing tests under tests/ document many integration contracts; add or adjust coverage with the implementation change.
